newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi jobless rate edges down to 6.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi jobless rate edges down to 6.4 pct.

text.p: Mississippi's unemployment rate rose slighty to 6.4 percent in August from 6.3 percent in July and 6.7 percent a year ago, the state Employment Security Commission said Monday.

"The August economy was somewhat sluggish," said Raiford Crews, state Chief of Labor Market Information. "The labor force conditions are still showing the effects of international trade agreements, which have contributed to the loss of 15,000 manufacturing jobs over the past 12 months."

Service industries added 4,900 jobs over the month and 6,200 jobs over the year. The largest anual increases came in amusements and casinos, which added 4,400 jobs; health services, which added 3,300 jobs, and government, which grew by 2,400 jobs.

"The next major factor affecting the economy will be the upcoming increase in the minimum wage rate," Crews said. "There is usually some job loss associated as businesses downsize to offset new wage standards."
Crews said the ensuing disruption to the economy is expected to be short term, and that Mississippi expects a reasonably strong economy over the next several months.
"There will be the usual seasonal changes as fall and winter weather conditions become part of the mix," Crews said.
Rankin County had the state's lowest unemployment rate in August, three percent, while Homes County had the highest, 19.5 percent.
